blocks.x: Standards we hold the build to, component by component:

items: Edge Silicon
Inference on the device where latency or bandwidth demands it — sized honestly for the workload.
Open Vino
Optimized inference on Intel silicon at the edge — models compiled for the hardware you own.
Sgx Enclaves Where Key Data Must Compute In Place
Computation inside hardware enclaves for the data that cannot move.
Hardware Telemetry Feeding Predictive Maintenance
Vibration, thermal and power signatures feeding models that schedule the technician.
Cost-Performance Benchmarking Per Workload Class
Workloads benchmarked on the axes that matter: latency, quality and cost together.
Delta / Iceberg tables
Open table formats underneath everything we build, so your data never belongs to a vendor.
data contracts
Typed schemas with owners and freshness expectations, agreed before a pipeline is allowed to ship.
dbt transformation graph
Tested, documented models with lineage exposure — the transform layer your analysts can actually read.
streaming ingest
Events land in seconds, not overnight batches — the precondition for decisions that happen in the moment.

blocks.x: Joint delivery on Intel Alliance is designed for handover from the first week — runbooks written as we go, decisions mapped to your owners, nothing that only we can operate.
Artifacts, not anecdotes — at the first-quarter close your team holds:

items: Joint architecture pack
The target architecture drawn against your estate, with interfaces and owners made explicit.
Certified delivery pod
A named team with the clearances your estate requires — the same people from diagnosis to handover.
Support map
Who answers when something breaks — named roles, response expectations and the escalation path.
